skill_friction: SKILL.md step 5 says to predict 'no preference' and decide instead of asking, but also allows the one intent message; with Q1 and Q3 predicted as no-preference yet load-bearing (license drives SharingSet profiles; agent path is a potential bypass), it is unclear whether bundling them into the one allowed message is correct or wasteful.

Rule 3's 'two wrong AskCoworker claims then verify every fact you keep' does not say how to count claims tagged [Proposal] (e.g., proposing an Update of a standard profile's object permissions) versus factual [Verified] claims; I counted the Guest-profile mislabel and the standard-profile editability claim as two.
The D2 split-retry rule ('a split sends both halves and counts as one retry') leaves the run.json kind ambiguous: both halves recorded as 'retry'.

design-rules 'security fix must not be bypassable by the same actor ... that is blocking' conflicts with a user 'no preference' answer that scopes out a channel (external agent) whose portal embedding cannot be verified with allowed commands; I marked it non-blocking with a recommendation, but the skill gives no rule for unverifiable bypass paths.

AskCoworker labelled facts from this run's own message as '[Verified: prior session]'; the skill treats 'prior session' as untraceable unless it appears in my message, which required per-fact cross-checking.
The spec format has no guidance on whether a SharingSet with multiple object access mappings is one row or one row per object; I used one component.
